title: GitHub Pages for Free Digital Product Store Hosting Explained for Digital Creators
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Selling ebooks, courses, templates, fonts, and digital downloads with automated crypto delivery — no platform middleman, no payout delays, no geographic filter.

content.text: If you're a digital creator in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, or any other country where Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, or Lemon Squeezy are severely restricted, you know the pain of losing income due to platform rejection or currency collapse. But what if you could sell your ebooks, courses, and digital products without relying on any of these platforms? Introducing GitHub Pages as a free digital product store hosting solution.
What This Actually Is and Why It Matters

GitHub Pages is a static website hosting service that allows you to deploy your digital product store without relying on any third-party platforms. This means you own your store, your accounts, and your data, giving you complete control over your digital business. By using GitHub Pages, you can avoid platform fees and restrictions, and focus on creating more value for your customers.
How the Architecture Works Under the Hood

The GitHub Pages architecture is built around a simple combination of free tools: GitHub Pages for hosting, Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOWPayments for automatic on-chain crypto payment verification. When a customer makes a purchase, the payment is verified on-chain, and the product is automatically delivered to their email address. This seamless experience is made possible by the integration of NOWPayments with Google Apps Script.
Who This Is Built For and Why

The product types that work with automated crypto delivery are any digital files that can be stored and delivered via download link: ebooks in PDF or EPUB format, courses packaged as ZIP archives or delivered via hosted video links, Notion templates exported as files or share links, font families as ZIP archives of OTF and TTF files, Lightroom or Capture One preset packs, beat files as WAV or MP3 archives, plugin installers, stock photo packs, software license keys, and any other file-based product. The delivery system in Stack 01 uses Google Drive shared links. Stack 02 uses Cloudflare R2 presigned URLs with configurable expiry times — typically 24 to 72 hours — which prevents download links from being shared indefinitely after a single purchase. Both approaches work reliably and cost nothing beyond the storage used.
Avoid platform fees and restrictions with GitHub Pages and the Sovereign Starter Stack.
The Components That Make It Work Together

The order management layer gives you complete visibility into every transaction your store processes. In Stack 01, every order is logged to a Google Sheet with the buyer's email, product purchased, payment amount in crypto and USD equivalent, transaction hash for on-chain verification, and delivery status. In Stack 02, orders are stored in a Supabase PostgreSQL database with the same fields plus additional metadata. Both can be exported as CSV at any time. The transaction hash provides cryptographic proof of every payment that does not depend on any platform's records — you can verify any transaction independently on a public blockchain explorer. This level of transparency and verifiability is structurally different from conventional payment processors, where transaction data is owned by the platform and subject to their record-keeping policies.
